niche.diet: Mineral slurries / chemosynthetic bacterial mats / dissolved iron

body: Armored carapace of iron-oxide plates, tube-like gill plumes, pressure-resistant gel-filled sinuses

links: Hard Fe2O3 armor replaces fragile calcite
chains.weakness: Heavy plates drain stamina in low gravity
observe: Water sizzles on contact with vent

plausibility.summary: Acidic, CO₂-influenced surface waters (F12) and impaired calcification (F13) push armor toward iron and silica phases; hydrothermal margins (F11) supply Fe²⁺/sulfide chemistry for iron oxide deposition. Heavy plates cost mobility on slopes—a real trade-off, slightly exaggerated at 0.97 g but still believable for a territorial, slow grazer.

links: 3.6 km depth exerts high hydrostatic pressure
Gel displaces water to equalize stress
Structural collapse prevented by fluid balance

skill.effect: Immunity to depth crushing, +10% movement on slopes

plausibility.summary: At ~3.6 km mean ocean depth (F10) hydrostatic pressure is large; gel-filled compartments and compliant tissues redistribute stress and avoid gas spaces—a well-known deep-sea design principle. Rapid ascent barotrauma as a weakness is physically honest.

links: Reliance on redox gradients from vents

plausibility.summary: Abyssal habitats lack usable sunlight; outsourcing redox metabolism to endosymbionts in gut or trophosome-like chambers is the standard vent solution. Hosting Taumoeba-like symbionts (F15, F16) that process exotic redox substrates is highly speculative in detail but fits the world's symbiosis canon and gameplay chemotrophy toggle.
